analysis.is_complaint_reason: The customer is dissatisfied, reports losing £650 to a scam and wants her money back, which meets the CH-1 definition of alleging financial loss.
analysis.summary: The customer paid a £650 deposit by bank transfer on 27/10 for a used car advertised on an online marketplace. The seller communicated over WhatsApp, sent photos and a fake logbook, and blocked her after payment. She reported it on 30/10 and wants her money back. This is a suspected authorised push payment (purchase) scam. She says she did not share bank security details. WhatsApp screenshots have been emailed in. She was asked about vulnerability and none was noted. The case must go to Fraud & Scams within 1 business day. Payee details, the payment time and confirmation of account security checks are missing.

timeline.event: Customer paid a £650 deposit by bank transfer to the car seller; the seller then blocked her
Customer reported the scam by phone; WhatsApp screenshots emailed in; asked about vulnerability

analysis.severity_reason: CH-6 sets suspected fraud or scam as High, even though the loss (£650) is in the Medium range.

vulnerability.suggested_support: None identified; the customer was asked. Stay alert to distress caused by the scam loss.

analysis.routing_reason: The customer was tricked into sending a payment to a fraudster (APP scam). ESC-1 and FRD-2 require a handover to Fraud & Scams within 1 business day.
